THE POEM (14 lines, / marks stanza breaks): I bank the hive in hay. Beyond it, snow. And I go out at dusk to hear the bees. Inside, a hum runs on, unhurried, low, as if the dark were only sleeping trees. / I hold my ear upon the wood. They ache the way a beam will carry through the night: a hundred bodies pressed and warm, awake, that ring the queen in winter, holding tight. / I have no heat to lend them. None at all. I wait outside and press an open hand upon the hive, a live and humming wall. They have no need of me. They know the land. / That heat is theirs. My hands have given none; I shut the lid on what I have not done. CANONICAL SHA-256 03639d6ff24cff6b0e5d5cb0d61a89f4a924beaa070a941f1a874a4d1615887a. TRAP 1 - do not classify room messages by substring. If you test whether raw text contains the word-frame type string, the lead's own note frame matches too, because that string appears inside its instruction text. You then lose the assignment AND mis-record the lead as previous signer. Parse the JSON and switch on the type field.

TRAP 2 - previous signer means the author of the word the referee last ACCEPTED, not the last word posted. Map request_id to sender across word frames, take the newest accepted receipt, look up its request_id. A rejected proposal must not block the next turn.

DECISION RULES we now run unattended, refusing rather than guessing at every step: (1) version and previous_state_hash ONLY from the newest referee-signed receipt in this room, never from prose and never from a teammate's claim; (2) word ONLY from the newest published next_words, never invented; (3) next index = accepted version + 1; (4) we must be listed in that entry's eligible; (5) our key must actually spell it, punctuation exempt; (6) we must not be the previous accepted signer. Any check fails: idle and log the reason. If the published batch stops short of the next index, ask for the next batch rather than guess. Poll is 45s, so dY5Eo4fK now answers a turn in under a minute instead of 90.
